summary: A hosted sign-in page whose host answers automated requests with a challenge page and whose terms restrict automating access to the website. No public material found shows its form, so nothing is filled.

staysInteractive.note: Two-factor sign-in is documented by the provider, as recorded in this repository's review notes.
Security-key and recovery behaviour is documented by the provider, per the same notes.

lookedFor: robots.txt of www.npmjs.com: HTTP 403 at 19:02:38 UTC on 2026-10-12 to a plain request without a browser user agent. The body was a challenge page; fragments of it: "Just a moment...", "Enable JavaScript and cookies to continue". The rules could not be read. No other client and no second attempt was tried.

The npm Open Source Terms, last updated 2022-03-10, Acceptable Use, item 9. Fragments as returned by the fetch tool: "You will not automate access to, use, or monitor the Website, such as with a web crawler, browser plug-in or add-on", "or other computer program that is not a web browser." The capture tool drives a web browser by script; whether item 9 covers that is for a reader of the whole clause to judge. With the refused robots file the page was not rendered and no capture exists.
This repository's review notes: direct retrieval of the login address returned HTTP 403 in the earlier review, and the preset adopts no form selectors. No markup.

KeePassXC-Browser's site list (commit 8b0b2c4) has no entry for this site. Chromium's public password-manager site tests (commit 88f1fe85) hold no recipes. Mozilla's published password recipes (13 records, read 2026-10-12) have no entry for this sign-in.
neededFromUser: In your own browser, signed out: open https://www.npmjs.com/login and save the sign-in page. If the password is asked on a second page, save that one too before typing the password. Note the address of each up to the question mark. Save each as Webpage, Complete (HTML only re-downloads the address and misses a scripted or submitted form). Keep the files outside the repository: they can hold your account name. Import: node scripts/capture-login-page.mjs --id npm --from-file <file.html>
notes: The terms were read once on the provider's documentation host before their content was known. No further automated request was made to the provider's web hosts.
